backgroundScene: Morrígan stands on a battlefield of the Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth in Avalora — a scarred plain of silver-root veins and broken standing stones. Colossal crow-feather totems rise from the ground, each taller than a tower, marked with fate-scarred prophecy. The labyrinth's thorn-walls are visible in the distance, their impossible geometry shifting like living thought. Battle-crow omens circle overhead in flocks that darken the sky. A cauldron of war-fate glows at the edge of the scene, its green-fire reflecting in her eyes. Mist veils drift across the battlefield, concealing and revealing the dead. The scene communicates: she IS the fate of warriors — the battlefield exists because she chooses who falls.
scaleCue: The crow-feather totems would be obelisks to humans but reach her shoulders. The standing stones are scattered like fallen chess pieces.
factionSkinLanguage: Living bark-silver skin with moonlit green-gold undertones. Thorn-vine patterns grow through the flesh like living tattoos. Fae glass fractures sparkle beneath the surface. Geas scars glow with silver-sidhe light. Mist-veil texture on the skin's surface — perpetually slightly out of focus, as if existing between mortal and fae. Root-lace patterns trace the nervous system in silver.
factionTraitDetails: Fae divine proportions — impossibly elegant, slightly elongated, with an unsettling beauty. The body changes slightly in peripheral vision — shapes shift, sizes seem wrong. Silver branch antler patterns can grow from brow and shoulders. Mist emanates from the skin continuously. The body feels ancient despite youthful appearance — thousands of years of memory in living wood.
